body.title: ci: free a Grok slot when the wake expires unclaimed or the task is done (-v3 of #494)
body.body:
Part of #411

Agent: vws-platform

AC: 1
AC: 2
AC: 3
AC: 4

## Rebuild (-v3 of #494, -v2 of #484)

Rebuilt as `ci/grok-wake-timeout-411-v3` by cherry-picking `d07e9be adb78aa ccbad13 f7c8ba5 31640e4` onto main `2f20db4`, without a rebase. #494 is closed with a link here. Conflicts:
- `.github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py` read allowlist (adb78aa): main added the `pulls/N/files` line (#397, Rule D serial set). Kept it and this PR's `timeline` addition on the `issues/N/(events|comments|timeline)` line.
- `decide()` auto-merged: this PR's `grok_released` state and extended `decide_grok(...)` call, then main's `decide_rebuild`, `grok_rework_actions` and `decide_lead` (#498) lines unchanged.
- Semantic conflict: main's rule AC (#492) added a module-level `AC_BOX_RE` for `AC: <n>` lines; this PR's later `AC_BOX_RE` (checkbox pattern) replaced it and broke `parse_ac` (`tests/orchestrate/test_ac_parity.py` failed 10 subtests on the cherry-picked head). New commit 63b2ad2 renames this PR's pattern to `AC_CHECKBOX_RE`.
- Checks on this head (box): tests/orchestrate 492 OK, workflows 104, drift 72, metrics 119, ci_fail 59, codex 23 OK (/workspace/handoff/factory/411/v3-green.log); pyflakes clean; `scripts/guard-agents.sh pr-commits origin/main HEAD` rc=0; `git diff --check` clean.
- The verdicts on #484 and #494 do not carry over.

## What changed

A Grok slot used to free only when someone closed the issue, removed `grok`, or unassigned it. Rule G now frees it in two more cases.

- `.github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py`:
  - New `ORCHESTRATE_GROK_WAKE_TIMEOUT_MIN` (default 120, positive integer).
  - `grok_release`: a woken issue that nobody claimed within the timeout frees its slot with the note `grok_wake_expired` (item, key, `woken_at`, `timeout_min`). A claim is an assignee, a non-marker comment after the wake, an `assigned` event after the wake, or a PR whose `Part of` names the issue.
  - A PR naming the issue merged after the wake, or every AC box ticked, frees the slot as `grok_task_done` (`pr_merged`/`ac_done`), even while assigned. This covers slots that were freed only by a manual close.
  - The note is logged once per key (`grok_released` in state). The issue is not re-woken with the same key; `/orchestrate reset-failures` or a new `ready`/`grok` label after the wake re-arms it (`grok_wake_key`).
  - `collect` takes the wake time from the wake-thread comments (`key_times`) and the claim from `GET issues/N/timeline` (`grok_activity`) of allowlisted open grok issues. The GET is added to the read allowlist. A read error keeps the slot.
  - The grok_wake action carries the released keys so the apply-time `recheck_grok` does not count them.
- `docs/factory-orchestrator.md`: the rule G row, the Grok re-check, and the new setting.

Prerequisites: #428 merged; #461 superseded by merged #467; #424 closed unmerged. Built on main.

Overlap: #491 merged as #498 (lead wake); this rebuild sits on top of it.

## How it was verified

- Failing first: /workspace/handoff/factory/411/failing-first.log. At the test commit, `tests/orchestrate/test_grok_timeout.py` gave 8 failures and 1 error. The review test commit failed with 1 error before its fix (review1-failing.log).
- tests/orchestrate 387 OK (/workspace/handoff/factory/411/green.log); tests/workflows 93, drift 69, ci_fail 54, codex 23, metrics 119 OK, run from the repo root as in CI (green-rest.log). pyflakes is clean.
- `scripts/guard.sh commits origin/main`: OK.
- Self review: /workspace/handoff/codex/411-self-review.md (2 rounds, 1 fix, blocking=0)

## Quality checklist (required)

AWS-grade production quality, not demo (see QUALITY.md). Every checked box needs evidence: a file:line, test name, command output, or link. Write "N/A: reason" where an item truly does not apply. An unchecked box without a reason means the PR is not done.

- [x] **Error handling**: a timeline read error gives `None` and the issue keeps its slot; a missing wake time keeps it too. Evidence: .github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py `grok_activity`; tests/orchestrate/test_grok_timeout.py `CollectTick.test_timeline_read_error_keeps_the_slot`, `Unclaimed.test_unknown_activity_or_wake_time_keeps_the_slot`
- [x] **Retries and timeouts**: no new retry loop. Each tick re-evaluates; the existing `Gh` timeouts and ETag cache cover the new GET. The wake timeout is configurable and validated. Evidence: .github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py:155, :271; `Config.test_default_and_validation`
- [x] **Security**: read-only. The only new endpoint is `GET issues/N/timeline`, added to the read allowlist; no new write. Orchestrator marker comments are not claims. Evidence: .github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py:372, :433; `CollectTick.test_marker_comments_are_not_claims`
- [x] **Unit tests**: expiry, within the timeout, claims (assignee, comment, assignment, linked PR), a comment before the wake, merged PR, a PR merged before the wake, AC done, re-arm by reset-failures and by a new label, and apply-time recheck. Evidence: tests/orchestrate/test_grok_timeout.py `Unclaimed`, `Claimed`, `Done`, `ApplyRecheck`
- [x] **Integration tests**: apply `tick`s through the stub `gh` expire once, then a comment claims the issue, marker comments do not, and a timeline 403 keeps the slot. Evidence: tests/orchestrate/test_grok_timeout.py `CollectTick`
- [ ] **vws-test live evidence (required)**: N/A: orchestrator on the factory box against GitHub only; nothing runs on the vws-test cluster
- [x] **Observability**: `grok_wake_expired` (item, key, woken_at, timeout_min) and `grok_task_done` (item, key, reason, pr) notes. Evidence: .github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py:1424 `grok_release`; `Unclaimed.test_expired_wake_frees_the_slot_and_is_not_rewoken`, `Done.test_merged_pr_frees_the_slot`
- [x] **Idempotency**: one note per key, kept in decision state; the same key is never re-woken, and the same plan results after a restart. Evidence: .github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py:1729; `Unclaimed.test_note_once_and_the_same_plan_after_a_restart`, `CollectTick.test_unclaimed_wake_expires_once_across_apply_ticks`
- [ ] **AWS compatibility (where applicable)**: N/A: no AWS API surface

vws-verify: FAIL on head 63b2ad2958588cc4a9156001b588bab0080eedcc (verify-wake run 20261024T164822Z-33ee39).

Codex review: /workspace/handoff/codex/vws-deploy-500-63b2ad2.md blocking=1

Codex high (CI orchestrator change), round 3/3 on #411. Tests pass at the head: tests/orchestrate 492 OK (test_ac_parity 3 OK, test_grok_timeout 17 OK), so the AC_CHECKBOX_RE rename fixes the semantic conflict with #492's parse_ac. Merge-tree against current main is clean.

Blocking:
1. .github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py:2367-2368 (grok_activity), used at :1702-1704 (grok_release): the blocker from the #494 FAIL is not fixed. This head is a cherry-pick of 31640e4, and a claim is still any non-marker comment after the wake, whoever wrote it. #411 AC1 says the claim is "an assignee/comment from the woken bot". One unrelated comment (a question from a person, another bot) means the wake never expires, and with the default Grok cap of 1 that blocks every later Grok wake. That is the stuck slot this PR is meant to fix, so the PR claims AC1 without meeting it. Codex rated this P2, but an unmet AC is a blocker under the review rules. Fix: keep the comment author (`e["actor"]["login"]` / `e["user"]["login"]`) in the timeline read and count a comment as a claim only when it comes from the woken bot's login (a config setting) or a current assignee. Add a failing-first test where an unrelated user's comment does not stop expiry.
2. .github/orchestrate/orchestrate.py:2372-2376 (grok_activity, cross-referenced PRs), used at :1696-1698 and :1702 (Codex P1, security): only the source repository `name` is checked, never its owner. The vws-* repos are public. Anyone can create a repo named e.g. `vws-iam`, open a PR there with `Part of #N` that references this issue, and merge it. That shows up as `grok_task_done` (pr_merged) and frees an occupied, assigned slot, which bypasses the Grok cap. An open PR there also counts as a claim and stops expiry. Fix: accept a cross-reference only when `source.issue.repository.owner.login == OWNER` (or `full_name` is `OWNER/vws-*`), and add a test with a foreign-owner cross-reference.

Non-blocking follow-ups (Codex P2): orchestrate.py:2885 (recheck_grok) subtracts `released` from the fresh occupancy without checking it. A task that expired at decide time but got an assignee or a linked PR before apply is still freed, so one extra wake can slip past the cap. Keep only `grok_task_done` releases there, or re-check expired ones against the fresh read. Also still open from #494: ignore cross-references that predate the wake or are closed unmerged.

The Codex cap for #411 is reached (round 3/3: #484, #494, #500). The next attempt needs a split (for example AC1's claim identity as its own issue) or a manual review. The verdicts on #484 and #494 do not carry over.
